subject: dvalincode
title: Narrowing-monotone org policy with canonical source-order-independent hash, enforced at a single tool chokepoint
one_why: Every resolution combinator only restricts (allowlists intersect, denylists union, caps take min, network takes the strictest level), so a repo-committed policy can never widen the machine policy -- tested property; sorted canonical resolution makes the resolved-policy hash source-order independent, which is exactly what a tamper-evidence hash needs; enforcement lives in one registry.run() chokepoint (tool deny -> per-target command/path checks -> approval -> audit) plus the MCP spawn path applying checkCommand itself because the chokepoint doesn't cover it.

subject: dvalincode
title: Un-raisable hard-block command class + allowlist-disqualifying shell constructs, matched per quote-aware command segment
one_why: Nuance on the permission-policy cluster: rm-rf-of-root, raw device writes, curl-pipe-shell and fork bombs are refused whatever the policy says -- no allowlist escape -- and any command containing substitution or redirection is disqualified from ever satisfying an allowlist because matching the visible text proves nothing about what executes; segmentation is quote-aware so 'ls && rm -rf ~' is caught as its segments.

subject: dvalincode
title: Hash-chained per-run audit log seeded with the policy hash, plus an offline verify command and an install-specific `trust` self-report
one_why: run_start records the resolved-policy hash + per-source hashes + git HEAD, each record chains prevHash over canonical JSON, verifyChain re-derives offline, and `dvalincode trust` prints the install's own posture (policy, per-surface network enforcement, MCP permissions, deps) so an approver verifies claims instead of trusting them; honest boundary stated in code: tamper-evident, not tamper-proof against a hostile local admin; shell_exec events deliberately carry the executable, never the arguments.

subject: dvalincode
title: Verified Fix Record: verdict from observed exit codes + independent re-scan, carrying its own gate rule so a third party can re-reach it; v1 keeps verifying under v1 rules forever
one_why: Inverts the standard 'ask the model that wrote the patch whether it is good': the record is executor-agnostic (dvalin/codex/claude-code/copilot/human), states narrowly (finding gone from this scan + checks observed to pass, never 'vulnerability-free'), and embeds the threshold+mode the verdict was reached under because two producers without it answered the regression question differently; the schema-versioning discipline -- v1 records permanently verify under v1 rules, since a record that stops re-deriving because the rules moved breaks the only promise the format makes -- is the corpus's most rigorous artifact-evolution stance.

subject: dvalincode
title: Append-only turn journal with idempotent replay and dangling-turn recovery, linked to the audit chain by ids and checkpoint hash only
one_why: Nuance on the seeded journal id: the journal is session state that may hold raw user text (so a crashed turn survives), while the audit chain never receives that content -- the two planes link only via runId/sessionId/audit-head hash, a clean separation most subjects blur by replaying through the same log.

subject: dvalincode
title: Triple-condition stall detector (exact-repeat, same-check-failing-without-edit, N-unverified-edits) with a one-nudge-then-stop escalation, plus first-edit investigation gate
one_why: Beyond crush's single breaker: three distinct stall signatures (consecutive identical action; the same focused check failing N times inside one write-generation; N consecutive writes with no read/diff/validation), each first answered by a single corrective nudge and only then a hard stop with a human-readable summary; the failed-test counter resets on any intervening source edit via a write-generation counter, which kills the retry-blind-backoff pattern without punishing legitimate re-runs.

subject: dvalincode
title: Trigger estimates the full outgoing request (messages + system + tool defs) at turn entry AND every iteration boundary, with a monotonic +1k-token anti-thrash guard between compactions
one_why: Nuance on the measured-input id: estimating includes serialized tool definitions so the number approximates the provider bill rather than chat text, the mid-tool-loop check keeps long turns from dying at the provider limit, and lastCompactionAtTokens + 1000 prevents summarize-thrash where compaction barely shrinks below the trigger; no usage feedback loop calibrates the char/4 estimate (mocode's edge), which is why this is nuance, not a new peak.

subject: dvalincode
title: Cache discipline as loop constraint: nudge messages append-only so every prior message stays cacheable, plus ephemeral cache_control on system/last-tool/last-block
one_why: Nuance on prompt-cache-marking: the interesting half is not the breakpoints but the loop-level rule -- the pending-work nudge is documented as appended specifically to keep the request prefix append-only -- and run_end records the cached/cache-miss/cache-write token split so cache behavior is observable per run, not just asserted.

subject: dvalincode
title: CI drives the built binary with the reference MCP client over a real pipe, with a require-flag that turns a missing build into a failure; a separate weekly job re-verifies against current real harness CLIs
one_why: In-process tests that build their own request strings cannot catch a protocol misread -- both sides would be wrong in the same way (a real regression here echoed the client's protocol version back); the fix is CI running an independent reference client against dist/, failing loudly if the build step was reordered away, plus a deliberately CI-external weekly job so interop claims carry a date instead of decaying silently in a PR comment.

subject: dvalincode
title: Offline meta-test asserting every third-party action's commit digest and its version comment never contradict each other across workflows
one_why: Dependabot moves digests and never the human-trusted version comments, so drift is silent; this test catches the repo contradicting itself -- one digest described two ways, or one version resolving to two digests -- which was the actual failure mode behind real breakages where two jobs of the same action landed on different commits and rejected each other at runtime; cheap supply-chain hygiene any MIT subject can copy today.
